chunks: Have you not considered those who were forbidden to conspire, but reverted after a time to what was forbidden them, and conspired evil, rebellion and disobedience to the Prophet? Yet when they come to you they greet you with a greeting even God does not greet you with; and say to themselves, 'Why doesn't God punish us for what we say?' Hell is sufficient for them, in which they will be burnt: And what an evil consequence!
ai.seo_question: Who are the people forbidden from al-najwa in Surah Al-Mujadila?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the hypocrites (Munafiqun) of Medina, particularly those who outwardly greeted the Prophet with 'As-Samu' (death) instead of 'As-Salam' (peace), reflecting their inner discord. The prohibition of 'al-najwa' (private counsel) specifically targets their secretive plotting against the community, while their internal monologue reveals a superficial belief that God only punishes for speech, ignoring the weight of their deeds. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the unity of inner intent and outer action in determining spiritual fate.
